claims.title: Exact linear function recovery by row-space inclusion
claims.scope: one sink receiving finite-field linear network symbols Gx and local side-information symbols Sx while demanding Bx
assumptions: source, network symbols, target functions, side information, and decoder operations use one declared prime field
the sink must recover every demanded function exactly for every source vector
nonclaims: the theorem does not cover nonlinear or approximate decoding without a new argument
finite-field rows are representations of internal information rather than parent-substrate ontology

claims.title: Conditional linear-demand cut lower bound
claims.scope: one sink with target rows B, local side-information rows S, and scalar finite-field symbols crossing every declared source-sink cut
assumptions: all source-dependent network information reaching the sink downstream of the cut is generated from the cut symbols
one cut unit carries at most one scalar field dimension per use
nonclaims: satisfying every receiver-wise cut bound is not claimed jointly sufficient for heterogeneous sinks
side information transmitted in an earlier stage must be counted in that stage rather than treated as universally free

claims.title: Exact bounded minimum common linear summary
claims.scope: bounded source dimension and prime field with finitely many linear sink demands and side-information row spaces
assumptions: the configured enumeration exhausts every independent generator set below the returned dimension
candidate subspaces are canonicalized by exact finite-field reduced-row-echelon form
the common message is a linear subspace basis sent before sink-specific decoding
nonclaims: a capped incomplete enumeration is not an optimum certificate
the result does not solve unrestricted nonlinear index coding or network function computation

claims.title: Receiver-wise cut adequacy is not joint heterogeneous-demand sufficiency
claims.scope: the declared two-bit one-symbol broadcast network with t1 demanding x1 and t2 demanding x2 and no side information
assumptions: the one shared source-to-relay edge carries one scalar linear form
both sinks receive only scalar multiples of that common form
both demanded basis functions must be recovered exactly
nonclaims: the counterexample does not say per-sink cuts are never sufficient under stronger common-demand assumptions
the obstruction is one shared scalar subspace rather than a general impossibility for larger block codes

claims.title: Restricted linear predictive-function bridge
claims.scope: finite predictive classes embedded explicitly in F_p^h with each sink's future answer signature declared as B_t x and side information as S_t x
assumptions: the embedding is injective on every predictive class distinction that remains relevant to the modeled sinks
the declared sink signatures are exactly linear in that embedding
recovering B_t x is sufficient for every future query assigned to sink t
nonclaims: arbitrary predictive functions need not be linear in a selected embedding
the finite-field class label is a coding choice rather than a physical identity

claims.title: Complementary side-information XOR broadcast
claims.scope: two binary source symbols, one common broadcast symbol, t1 knowing x1 and demanding x2, and t2 knowing x2 and demanding x1
assumptions: the relay copies one common source symbol to both receivers
local side information is exact and causally available at decoding time
nonclaims: the result does not make side information free under every accounting system
one XOR construction is not a general index-coding theorem

claims.title: Exhaustive binary side-information broadcast separation
claims.scope: all 16 local binary scalar coefficient assignments in the declared one-source relay-broadcast network
assumptions: the finite assignment domain consists of four source edge vectors and two scalar choices on each relay-to-sink edge
routing-only source messages are zero or unchanged source basis symbols
the search cap exceeds the complete 16-assignment domain
nonclaims: the finite search does not rule out models outside the declared scalar assignment space
a capped search is reported incomplete rather than impossible
